# Group frontier, families246–259

7 October2026. Worker frontier_groups, GPT-6.1 Sol/max; no nested workers. Release pinned at `adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a`. Three complete manuscripts read: *Finite algebraic envelopes and the Boone–Higman conjecture* (35pp,23 September), *A universal group of type F∞* (18pp,same date), and *Strong Ulam Stability Characterizes Amenability* (19pp,5 October). Two companions were read only at their introductions/metadata;247 at three complete selected sections. The other assigned families remain catalogue depth.

The strongest outcome is a set of exact tools and obstructions that do not require accepting the release's global breakthroughs. Full proofs are in [STRUCTURAL_TOOLS.md](</Users/harjas/Documents/ChatGPT/Literature Digestion/notes/frontier_groups/cycle19/STRUCTURAL_TOOLS.md>) and [ULAM_TOOLS.md](</Users/harjas/Documents/ChatGPT/Literature Digestion/notes/frontier_groups/cycle19/ULAM_TOOLS.md>). No literature-priority claim or external validation is made.

## Exact deductions

| Tool | Interface and conclusion | Use and boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Rank-four r-ary kernel theorem | For an associative unital ring R and possibly nonunital coefficient endomorphism ψ, r equivalent orthogonal corners commuting with ψ(R) make ψ(ker(St₄→E₄)) central of exponent dividing r−1. Binary splitting kills it; two splitting arities with coprime r−1 kill it as well, without cross-system commutation. | Four coordinates suffice for this kernel mechanism. Proof uses actual Steinberg relations, not just equality of matrices. No rank-three claim. |
| Smaller affine envelope | Conditional on family250 Theorem2.2's algebra package and the imported Krstić–McCool finite-presentation theorem, replace B⁶⋊St₆ by B⁴⋊St₄. Faithfulness, two-transitivity, stabilizer finite generation and input embedding survive. | Root positions decrease30→12; translation generators6→4. This does not validate the programme compiler or establish a smaller F∞ construction. |
| Sharp finite-matrix barrier | For d×d complex matrices, the least possible maximum norm error in `tᵢsⱼ=δᵢⱼI`, `Σsᵢtᵢ=I` is `max{1/r,(r−1)/(r+1)}` for every d. Adjoint contractions attain it. | Binary splitting cannot be approximated below1/2 in this norm, however large d becomes. A rank proof rules out any nonzero exact finite-dimensional corner over every field. |
